summary: legal checked in 6 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for public launch of searchwoot.com; counsel_required for any Woot rights-dependent public display, alert expansion, affiliate, or advertising use. Exact decision: keep searchwoot.com private, keep outreach unsent, and permit only bounded read-only evidence work. Woot API documentation establishes access mechanics but not redistribution rights; current terms restrict commercial/public use, storage, derivatives, listings, prices, and data mining. Security, accuracy/freshness, measurement, attribution, privacy, consent, vendor, incident, and owner gates remain incomplete. Ordinary reversible growth elsewhere remains conditional when it preserves existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, platform-policy, and data boundaries. Incomplete telemetry alone is not a legal blocker.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active: 0 of 4 tasks closed and 4 remain open. Existing progress is evidenced by Woot API, terms, support, repository/configuration, privacy, cookie-policy, and draft-terms artifacts. No task closes because rights, field permissions, retention, deletion/correction/access workflows, notification consent, GA4 settings, vendor coverage, incident procedures, accuracy/freshness, and rollback evidence remain incomplete. Next evidence action: attach and review one consolidated read-only bundle covering the field-level rights matrix, deployed data-flow and retention table, log/vendor/incident inventory, consent and GA4 configuration evidence, accuracy/freshness controls, and rollback evidence.

Data-use review dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data — blocked; user alert rules and sync results — evidence_needed; GA4 analytics — evidence_needed; operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data — evidence_needed. Smallest next actions: complete the internal Woot counsel packet before any owner-authorized outreach; produce the read-only deployed/repository data-flow and retention table; capture deployed consent/withdrawal and GA4 property settings without enabling tracking; produce the read-only log, vendor, and incident inventory. No go-live approval is supported.

Fleet compliance is a technical baseline, not certification: 35 sites pass, 18 fail, and 6 are unknown, with open banner, consent, GA4, privacy, and terms findings. Data quality is yellow for analytics source permissions or collector errors; revenue covers one day only and includes $4.92 aggregate commission that cannot be assigned to a site. Do not treat unavailable telemetry or unattributed revenue as zero. Continue ordinary reversible work only within existing consent, disclosure, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and age-sensitive boundaries.

For the parked scaffold sites, preserve private/parked status. The concrete next evidence action is to attach dated execution-owner verification, preview/build evidence, compliance and security checks, measurement boundary, rollback point, and explicit blocker for each existing owner-gap work item. Do not publish, deploy, alter DNS, configure analytics, monetize, or spend before those gates are evidenced.

Maintain the existing private launch gates. Fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results, all security sitefacts remain unknown, and material access, secrets, isolation, release, dependency, TLS, data-exposure, monitoring, incident, and disclosure controls are unevidenced. Ordinary bounded growth may continue conditionally; security-sensitive public exposure remains blocked.
